units.translation: - 718 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧, through the supplication. The story of Ixion, the first murderer and first ⟦3⟧ (so more correctly ⟦4⟧; cf. Welcker ⟦5⟧), A. had treated in the ⟦6⟧ and the ⟦7⟧, probably as it is presented in Diodorus 4, 69; at least there, as in A. (Frg. 88 in Schol. ⟦8⟧), Ixion's father was called Antion. Ixion had lured his father-in-law Eioneus, to whom he owed the bride-price (cf. ⟦9⟧. Frg. 184) and who had seized his horses as security, to him under false promises of payment and pushed him into a pit filled with fire (Frg. 185). No one wanted to purify him for this murder; then he became a suppliant of Zeus (Frg. 340 ⟦10⟧). According to Frg. 381 (⟦11⟧ according to Reitzenstein's manuscript of the Etym. M.), the murderer had also, to secure himself against revenge (similarly as through the ⟦12⟧, at ⟦13⟧), taken blood from the murdered man into his mouth and spat it out. Yet Zeus took pity on this wicked murderer and purified him; but he repaid it by trying to seduce Hera, and for that he came to the wheel. So, say the Erinyes, Zeus certainly acted wrongly in accepting this ⟦14⟧, who repaid him thus: ⟦15⟧ "you say it" (so correctly Wilamowitz), as in the Gospel ⟦16⟧ "you say it", a form of affirmation where for some reason one does not want to assert openly (more fully Phaedra in Hippolytus 352 ⟦17⟧, ⟦18⟧). One would like to know how in the drama the so entirely undeserved grace of Zeus was motivated. But it is incomprehensible to me how critics (Merkel, earlier Weil, Wecklein) could have destroyed this close connection between 718 and 719 by transposing 719-23 after 730. The chorus, out of respect, does not go further into this matter and repeats (with the same expressions) its first threat.
until with sprinklings of blood of a slain pig Zeus himself purifies you, pouring it over your hands
not having obtained a victorious outcome

721 ff. Apollo: that you will lose will happen; for you count for nothing, of course not among (⟦1⟧, see Wecklein) the younger gods, to whom you do not belong, but also not as one of the older ones (cf. what he said at 69f.). Thereupon the chorus: that will then be a counterpart to what you accomplished in the case of Admetus.
